text: DO NOT BUY THIS INSURANCE! Given my experience, I have to say this is probably the worst insurance agency I've ever dealt with in my life. I have open complains with the BBB and CA Department of Insurance against them, and I'm contemplating litigation at this point since they seem to not give a flying rip about me. My decent into pet insurance hell began on Christmas Eve of 2019, when my dog began vomiting uncontrollably. The vet diagnosed my dog with a possible bowel obstruction and he also noticed a suspicious mass, so my dog underwent an exploratory abdominal surgery and had the mass removed and biopsied. What a Christmas! I don't have a wife or kids, so this dog is like a child to me. My dog's bowels were cleared, but the mass turned out to be an aggressive mast cell cancer. This led to many follow up visits and medications that cost several thousands of dollars. To start off with, Pets Best said it would take them a MONTH before they even bothered to look at my claim. So I had to eat thousands of dollars in medical bills with the expectation that I would possibly get reimbursed over a month from the time they were filed. Well, a month goes by and they finally get around to looking at my claim. I get a nice little rejection letter by email in the middle of the night on a Friday (so I have to wait the entire weekend before I can talk to anyone) telling me that my claim was rejected because my vet wasn't giving them the required medical records. So of course I call my vet and make sure all the appropriate records were sent, then call Pets Best to confirm they got the records - and Pets Best said they did! Yet they continued to reject my claims saying they never got my records! I've called repeatedly both my vet and Pets Best trying to clear this up, same response every time. This nonsense is still going on today! I just got another rejection record for my last claim on 3/2/2020 for the same reason. I still haven't been paid for the initial claim on 12/24/2019! This business is a scam! I've filed complaints with the California Department of Insurance and the Better Business Bureau against them. I'm giving them time to respond to those complaints before I open litigation against them. These people need to be shut down. My claim aside, the way I was treated by them was also outrageous. When they reject your claim, they do so by issuing an automated email, typically in the middle of the night when they know you can't reach anyone, instead of notifying you by phone, so you can't dispute it with them directly. I tried getting the contact information for their VP of claims or the GM and they refused to let me talk to them. When I tried to escalate my issue up the chain of command over the phone, they transferred me to a supervisors voice mail who never bothered to call me back! This place is a joke! ----- Update: So Ali here gets back to me and says they are missing some specific records from a vet I visited back in 2018. None of the other customer service agents I talked to ever mentioned this to me. This is the first I've heard of it! I asked SEVERAL customer service agents REPEATEDLY if there was anything missing and I was told NO! I had to post a public Yelp review before they bothered to tell me what they were even looking for! So here we go again! I called my old vet and they said they don't have the records that Pets Best is looking for. My old vet said they faxed over all the records they have on file, so now my old vet has to try and figure out a way to amend finalized notes from years ago to satisfy Pets Best. This is crazy. ----- Update: Their Assistant VP of sales just got back to me after I filed all of these complaints and went public with my problems. She has assured me that she is personally looking into the case and will work with my vets to get the information they need. Hallelujah! The question you have to ask yourself is, why didn't they work with my vets to get this resolved in the first place?! Why didn't they tell me specifically what records they were looking for when I called the last several times? Why do they send automated rejection letters instead of hold notices that explain exactly what information they feel is missing? While I'm supremely grateful that I finally have senior management looking into my case, I have to question what kind of operation they are running over there. ----- Update: You're not going to believe this one! They finally finished reviewing my case. They claimed the exploratory abdominal for the suspected bowel obstruction... was wait for it... DENIED - BECAUSE THEY SAID IT WAS ACTUALLY A SURGERY FOR A PRE-EXISTING LIVER CONDITION!!!!!! - No, I'm not joking. I swear, check out the photo! I really need to sue these people. These people are disgusting.

text: If it hadn't been for the sweet waitress, the sangria and the deviled egg flight, I would have liked to give this place less than one star. In a nutshell, every dish was served cold. Most of it under-seasoned and simply bland. And dry... Sahara desert dry... There are heaps of the less expensive items on the plate (grits, potatoes, cornbread), in sharp contrast to the diminutive nature of the more expensive items (salmon, asparagus). I actually apologized to my foodie for bringing them here. Some assorted details: The deviled egg flight was fabulous. Each egg filled and garnished in a different way. Pleasing to the eye and the palate. $10 a bit steep for 5 half eggs, but it's Carmel, so it's expected. The cornbread. Huge portion of it... 4 big squares... this at least had some flavor, but also on the dry end of things. A bit of butter and bit of Pimiento cheese accompanies this cornbread appetizer. The fried green tomato and black-eyed pea fritters. For $11 you get three slices of tomato and 4 little fritters. The dips are great, the fried green tomatoes also quite tasty. The black-eyed pea fritters not so much. After biting into one, you find the center has the consistency of re-fried beans, but cold and tasteless. I wish they would just sell the tomatoes in a separate dish, because I will not ever eat those fritters again. So let's discuss the main dishes. Grits, cheesy grits... I was so looking forward to those... what I got was a mountain of some substance that clearly had corn in it, but was more the consistency of... darn I can't even think of anything that I would willingly eat with that consistency... It was a huge lump of cold, dry, hard tasteless something with bits of corn showing. There were some black beans on my plate also and they were cold but tasty, so I do recommend those. I also had two pieces of fried banana on my plate and they were delicious. Wish I had more of those. My friend who had also ordered the same dish did not receive any bananas. The salmon seemed tiny on the mountain of grits. Nice grill marks though... a little too much actually as those were seared halfway through the salmon and tasted simply burned. Welcome to cold hard unseasoned burned salmon. The chili lime butter did nothing to combat the situation as the grits soaked it up like a sponge in record time. My friend's salmon was in the same condition as mine. All my guest that had ordered dishes with asparagus received 4 extra skinny half stalks of it. That in itself would be ok, but it looks ridiculous when you lay that across 5 pounds of grits or mashed potatoes that are on the plate. Unfortunately the meatloaf didn't fare any better than the salmon, but there was a more generous portion of it on the plate... unfortunately... nobody really wanted more of it. It's a giant cube of meatloaf, which apparently has to have one or more sides that are completely burned. and of course it kept with the theme of cold, dry and bland. The slow roasted pork... per my guest... evoked memories of her childhood's school cafeteria... cold, dry, bland... The mashed potatoes were deemed to be ok by some of my guests. In my opinion this is great if you want to hang out on the patio on a nice night, sip some drinks and share some apps. Otherwise... NO

text: Hands-down the best restaurant ever! I have been to many places to eat and somehow I always find myself comparing anywhere I go to the experience I have when I go to Bricktop's. They're not like everywhere else where one server only watches a section and they are fully responsible. Yes they have sections, but every server covers other servers. I can't preach enough about how if every restaurant structured their service like Bricktop's does their ratings would go through The roof. I could go on and on about this place bc there's a unique history and culture with BrickTop's. There use to be another famous restaurant in this exact location before BrickTop's; it was called "Houston's", and when it closed down, 1 of the 4 previous owners (Joe Ledbetter) started BrickTop's titled from an inspirational place in Paris he likes to go eat... So if you ask me what my favorite dish is, I can't answer bc they are all amazing (even the sushi); but if I had to choose I'd get one of their featured prime steaks with their staple "twice baked potato" ...maybe some deviled eggs & sugar bacon or a fresh side salad. text: This is probably my favorite veterinary hospitals I've ever been to. We had to make the worst decision of our lives...whether or not to euthanize our sweet cat, Skippy. A WEEK PRIOR...... to going to Baring Boulevard our 4 year old male DLH cat Skippy started throwing up. He was vomiting more than 20 times in a 24 hour period. Every time he would throw up he would scream out in pain. At first we thought he just had the stomach flu and was screaming out in pain from the force of throwing up. When he did vomit, all that came up was foam and maybe a little clear/water like fluid. He started to loose his fur in chunks and always secluded himself and didn't want to be near anyone. We were crushed to say the least. But we started to document everything. He wasn't eating. He didn't eat for 5 days. He wasn't drinking the last 24 hours. He stopped throwing up and was sleeping more and more. We made an appointment with our local vet who happened to never return our calls and that's when we decided to go to Baring Boulevard Veterinary Hospital with no appointment When we walked into the hospital the first thing we saw was the reception area. I was with my 12 year old and 10 year old girls. The receptionists up front were super nice and made us feel more than welcome. I believe within 4 minutes we were taken back. The exam that my cat Skippy received was called an "end of life" exam. Quite frankly the name of the exam scared the cr** out of me. It was explained to me what it all meant. The veterinarian actually did a detailed exam. It was extremely detailed. They checked Skippy to see how his heart,lungs ears, teeth and mouth were. I told the veterinarian all the details.There was a blockage.... When she checked Skippys temperature it was low. Heart rate was lower than normal. It was around 98 degrees. His gums and skin and everything else showed kidney and liver issues which was a irreversible issue that happens when you don't eat for 5 days or drink for 24 hours. She said the kidney and liver function was depleted and would recover from that alone. We were given options, all of which SUCKED. ONE OPTION....Get a slew of blood tests to see what was going on and xrays to see how bad the blockage was. If needed, he would need surgery to remove any blockage but would still not live too long because of the liver and kidney issues. We would be looking at upwards of $1000 and he still would have liver and kidney issues. SECOND OPTION....Take skippy home and let him pass away there. He would probably become septic and pass from that. Could be months and he would be in pain till that time. THIRD OPTION.....Do a humane euthanasia on him. OUR DECISION....It took us quite a while to decide what it was we wanted to do. My girls and I talked and then we called to speak with my husband and my son who were at home. We went with what we felt was our only option......we chose to euthanize. We asked a while slew of questions about the process and what Skippy was going to feel and things like that. The veterinarian left us alone for as long as we wanted in the exam room to say our goodbyes. Let me start off with saying the "end of life" exam room was gorgeous. They had a comfortable bench and on the exam room table their was a soft and cuddly animal blanket with tissues and bottles of water. It was beautifully done. The window had a a blind on it so you have peace and quiet and privacy during this time. What I enjoyed the most and thought was the greatest of all was the fact that the vet told my kids what she was going to do and why In Age appropriate language. I as a mother chose to allow my youngest who is 10 to watch the sedation part of it but not the final step, euthanasia. PLEASE NOTE:This whole time the veterinarian was super sweet and was petting my sweet Skippy cat and talked to him and went to a deep level with him. She was not only amazing with our sweet boy, but she was extremely professional and kind with us all. She, the veterinarian made it such a wondering experience. I recommend Baring Boulevard Veterinary Hospital to any and everyone. I also called around for prices before we went here. They were by far the cheapest around. For my whole visit we spent End of life exam-$79 Euthanasia-$69 Disposal of Skippy-$40 Total it was $188

text: I came here for restaurant week and I was also celebrating my anniversary with the Mr.! This is the perfect place for a date or more romantic dinner! Especially since it is tapas style and you can share plates/try different things. Friends and groups are definitely welcomed, but the ambience with candlelight lighting (and wine bottle selection!) have total date vibes for trying to impress someone. Restaurant week First Course: We ordered Serrano ham, manchego cheese, olives, and the paprika garlic chorizo! Wow, the chorizo was flavorful and seasoned perfectly. All items complimented each other. The first course is served with a little bread too Second course: We orders the duck montadito, Pulpo (octopus!), the green beans, and beef brochettes. The beef brochettes were tender beef skewers, and octopus was on point in their thick marinade. The winners for the course was surprisingly the duck! I don't believe this is a regular menu item but if you get the chance, definitely order it!! It was incredibly rich and served on a small piece of baguette with a sweetened cherry. All the flavors complimented each other and reminded me how delicious duck can be when done right! Last, the green beans may be the best green beans I ever had. They were served with almonds, in a balsamic vinaigrette-oil with additional seasoning that were absolutely delicious. You know if they make green beans as it's own dish, then they have to be pretty incredible. Dessert: goat cheese flan and an ice cream yogurt fruit dish! Absolutely delicious, light and sweet. We were also served two sweeten pears at the end of the meal as a last goodbye treat. Overall the food was incredible! Service was really quick, if I had to give one negative it is the size of the tables. Especially with tapas, there were a lot of plates and little space. Everything else was stellar. When making the reservation, I noted it was for an anniversary dinner... to my grateful surprise the restaurant gave us complimentary champagne for the celebration! It was greatly appreciated and thoughtful. Restaurants that go that extra step is why this place deserves the five stars!

text: Chicken tika - tender cubes, pleasant but mild sweetness Chana masala, medium - good portion, tasty, good spice level Samosas - hot AF Rice generous helpings I ordered from Kurinji for the first time the other day and was definitely pleased. The first thing that leapt out at me was that holy heck, the samosas were spicier than anticipated! That wasn't a problem, though, and I enjoyed both - nice, crisp outside, spicy pea-and-potato goodness within. The accompanying chutney and sauce were also good quality. The chickpeas were a great spice level, though to my surprise a bit milder than the samosas. The portion was on-point and the taste was strong and good enough that I didn't regret passing on my usual habit or ordering lamb or seafood when I eat Indian. It went excellent with the rice, naturally. The tika, meanwhile, was genuinely mild (which is what we wanted), creamy, and mildly sweet, with wonderfully tender chicken breast cubes. If nothing quite reached mind-blowing, it was an excellent meal made of two main dishes and naan that tasted exactly like we were hoping they would, and a nice surprise in the seasoning of the samosas.

text: I've many times enjoyed Twenty Four Blackbird's sweet, smaller-than-standard size, and adorably packaged chocolate bars, so when driving past Santa Barbara, I made a quick stop at their very own brick and mortar space. It was an easy and quick five minute detour off Highway 1. There did not appear to be a designated parking area, but we arrived right at opening time, so were able to snag a spot along the street right in front of the store. Even from outside it's a beautiful space, with a wood framed storefront and big windows, but inside, it is truly stunning. Dark, without being too moody, again with lots of swirly-grained wood, live plants, and gorgeous displays. The back wall showcases each of their bars along with a companion jar for samples and tasting. At the front desk, you will find their bon bons and some other goodies. They offer the option of putting together a special box with your choice of five bars and eight chocolates, and it is discounted generously, but as the bars are available at stores in my hometown, but the chocolates can only be procured here, I opted to select just the latter (at $3 each). Chocolates are mostly either ganache or caramel filled; featuring perfectly tempered dark chocolate shells hand painted with colorful whirls, speckles, or other artistic touches. We had the following: Espresso Ganache - Very strong coffee flavor and not super sweet. Rosemary Caramel - After my first bite I exclaimed, out loud, "oh, wow." The rosemary is VERY noticeable, and I love it! It pairs perfectly with the dark, almost burnt loose caramel. This is a fantastic chocolate! Not PB and J - Like the best grown up PB cup ever, but with a salty-sweet firm sunflower seed butter. Lavender ganache - They clearly have the infusing skill down. This bon bon has a lavender flavor that is present, but not overwhelming. It's a good lavender, too: mild, floral, not too resinous or acerbic. Bits of blossoms revealed themselves as the ganache melted, adding a touch of texture. Togaroshi Caramel - Their caramel should be held up as the Goldilocks standard: nearly burnt, but saved at the last second, soft, but not so much that it runs out of the shell when bitten. Paired with togaroshi, this is truly spicy, but it works! Cacao fruit pate - Really interesting and creative. Cacao juice does not taste like chocolate, as one might expect. Instead, it's just a mild sweetness with a hint of something familiar, maybe molasses? The woman who assisted us was so fun and enthusiastic (plus super stylish and just plain cool). She took the time to mark my selections on a flavor key, and even went out of her way to suggest some places to visit and dine in the area. We were both super charmed by her, and she really made the experience special. In fact, she noticed that my husband was most excited about the espresso ganache, so gave us samples of their espresso cacao nib brittle, and of course, he loved it so much that we had to get a bag of that as well!

text: Just like Benihana, another over-exaggerated trendy restaurant, but in a form of a steakhouse promising unparalleled service and cuisine. Came here on my birthday, and from what I understand, plans are made in advance and the staff was aware. Now I wasn't expecting Fourth of July sparkling bottles of Cristal being walked to my table by scantily clad women, but I sort of expected, at least an offer, of something like a complimentary glass of wine. For the amount of money this place rakes in, I just found it really tacky. Although, they were gracious enough to dump confetti on my table. Happy birthday me. Other than the happy birthday confetti, it was no different than being just a regular customer. they actually moved us out of the main dining room closer to the bar per our request. We browsed the menu and after some time made our selection. I ordered the "celebration surf and turf" with 2 cold water lobster tails and an 8 oz. filet mignon per recommendation of the waitress. I ordered my steak 'blue', as per the norm. As we continue to imbibe, with not even so much as an offer of a cheap well drink, our main course comes. Oh, going back to my pictures, I remembered we ordered butterflied shrimp for an appetizer, but it's apparent that they weren't nothing spectacular if I can't really remember without seeing a picture I took of them. Thinking back, they were actually the best thing we had eaten and the entire restaurant that night. Anyhow, getting back to the steak, my steak isn't exactly blue, it's more on the medium well side. Okay. That's fine. I'm hungry, and I'm already basically discouraged and disappointed at this place. So I just stay quiet and eat my steak, patiently awaiting my lobster tails. As I see the waitress make a few trips to tables around our vicinity, I decide to ask her when they will come out. She then tells me that she didn't know I ordered lobster tails with my meal, even though SHE WAS THE ONE WHO SUGGESTED IT. So, I'm basically done with my steak, now I'm waiting for my lobster tails. Notice I said tails, as in plural, as in two. A little bit of time goes by, and here comes A SINGLE LOBSTER TAIL. Me, being gullible and optimistic, only because this is supposed to be a five-star high-class restaurant, I'm guessing my other lobster tail is on its way. I finished my lobster tail, and pull the waitress again and ask her where my other lobster tail is. She then asks me if I want another one. at this point, having been there two hours, I just said F*** it, and said no. We finish gallivanting and drinking our cocktails, and the check comes. Guess how my (not) "surf and turf" meal was broken down? Item-by-item. So instead of paying for a meal that I think was around 60 bucks, it came to about 80, maybe more if I remember right. The actual amount isn't important, it's the fact of the matter that the lack of attention paid to me, especially on my birthday, let alone a regular customer is unacceptable, and breaking down my meal item by item. I don't know if she was new, or if she was just overwhelmed, but I still can't wrap my mind around how you suggest a meal configuration, that I immediately order, and you not only get it wrong, but you bill me as if I ordered all a la carte items! Enough of that, let's get to the food. For all this decades-long praise and positivity about this place, especially amongst entertainers, and high-profile people alike, it sort of makes me wonder if any of these people have ever been somewhere other than Denny's and McDonald's in their life? The steak, like I said, overcooked, but the filet mignon although tender, is the least flavorful cut of steak. Ask a butcher. When I mentioned that to the waitress, she kind of sneered at me. Obviously not knowing who I am or knowing what I know, or knowing how much I cook. Other than that, it was just a filet mignon, nothing special, and definitely DEFINITELY not something I would go back for. Matter of fact, if I ever did go back, which I can probably guarantee you right now I never will, I would never order it again. The lobster tail, was indicative of being cooked in a hurry. And I also noticed as I was waiting on my lobster, other tables were getting theirs. Kind of chewy and rubbery on the ends, but slightly palatable in the center. And I forgot to mention, when I ordered initially I ordered extra lemon and butter, which I didn't get until I was almost finished with it. Now I don't know who made the mistake on my order, whether it was the believably knowledgeable waitress, or the kitchen, but I just know it was wrong, and I am not impressed, and I will not go back to a Ruth's Chris ever again. As a matter of fact, I went to outback for the first time in 15 or 20 years, and their food and service completely blows Ruth's Chris out of the water. text: Visited the wknd of 10/3/20 for the grand (re)opening of their dining room, post-quarantine. My (new) partner took me here for my first visit and what an opportunity to try this gem. Masks are required at all times except when seated at your table (good!). Staff are all PPE'd as well. Tables are at least 10' and more typically 12+ feet apart which left occupancy appearing to be less than 50 percent. Tough times = tip well! We started with a Jamaica Dove (tequila and hibiscus with salted/sweet rim)... such a delightful cocktail we ordered another. The Sonoran/UNESCO menu was a prix fixe at $35 and consisted of one choice from a small grouping in each of the following categories: appetizers; entrees; and desserts (see pic of menu). The carne asada tostadas (two 3-inch chilled tostadas) were incredible... so many different flavors and colors adorned this little work of art and, for me, was the highlight of an incredibly competitive menu. She had the Hamachi Aguachile - another chilled appetizer that was at once sweet and subtly tart. The Hamachi fish was thin, tender and delicate. For entrees we ordered the Grilled Cortez Shrimp with corn tamale and calabacitas and the Roasted pork shoulder with black beans and caramelized cabbage. The shrimp were very large and there were 6-7... plenty. The pork shoulder was equally ample and absurdly tender/good. For dessert we got the dark chocolate ganache and the panna cotta with pineapple compote and passion fruit (pics of all posted). The whipped ganache was dark/bitter and balanced by dollops of lightly sweetened whipped cream. It was too large to finish after the entrees and we took half home (and they tasted excellent the next day). The panna didn't fare as well and was finished in minutes... extremely sweet (almost too) but saved by equal extremes of tartness... almost keylime-esque. This would pair very well with espresso. Parking is ample in the free/small side lot. It was 4/5 full on this Saturday evening despite the limited occupancy. This was never sufficient when Zayna's used to occupy this location and likely won't be sufficient once the quarantine lifts. I'm worried about the front windows being blocked. I didn't see any signs posted prohibiting parking (and no one had to this wknd) but it would ruin the ambience if people started parking right in front of the main windows. Zayna's prohibited it and they were vigilant about it, to great credit and appreciation once inside. Bathrooms (2) are unisex, elegant, and spacious and even feature a baby changing station. Decor is rustic/elegant with an eye-catchingly massive (12-15 foot) cholla skeleton mounted on the far wall. I look forward to returning here soon!

I ate and ate and ate and all was good. And then, like a siren at sea, the Dessert Island called me over and I began my final phase of this extensive delicious research. The chocolate mouse cake melted in my mouth, the rice pudding, the cotton candy, and the Gelato, I'll never forget the Gelato (blows dessert island a kiss ,, I'll see you again very soon desert island 3) Let's not forget the service. I loved how the place was full but did not feel packed, every seat is a good seat and every dish is a great choice By far, my best Reno Buffet experience.

Sometimes, it can be overwhelming to choose something. Luckily, the signage throughout the store can help you figure out what you're into. Beside each oil and vinegar, there are suggestions of what foods are best paired with these. I also find that the staff are usually available to help you find what you're looking for. Another plus is that they have different sizes of bottles to choose from. If you're trying out a new flavour you can buy the smallest size. If you have a tried and true favourite, you can buy the largest bottle. They even have gift sets available. My family loves these Evoolution products and have been using them for years. Using these oils and vinegars have elevated my salad eating experiences at home. The bottles look so classy compared to your average grocery store salad dressing. The coolest part is that these oils and vinegars can be used for many other foods such as meats, cheeses, ice cream and popcorn! If you haven't been in one of these stores, I totally recommend checking one out!

text: Circles is my shizzzzzz! Ice cream and local businesses are two of my all time favorite things so I was immediately drawn to Circles. I first tried a few flavors at a Yelp event and was instantly impressed with the quality of the mix-ins. They were just as flavorful and well-made as the ice cream itself and added the right textures to make each spoonful more addicting than the last. The collabs with other local businesses like Hotel Tango, Tinker Coffee Co., and New Fangled Confections make this the ice cream of choice for Indy lovers. I've tried several flavors by now and am always blown away. The creativity and quality demonstrated by the makers behind Circles exceeds that of Ben and Jerry's... I'm not kidding, it's that good. The packaging of the pints and the social media presence is also super trendy and eye-catching. I only wish it was easier to get your hands on a pint since it's not sold in stores (yet?). They do offer delivery on many Saturdays, but I haven't tried that yet. They occasionally have pick up days at Wildwood Market and at events like the Yelp Bazaar and other makers' markets. I'm proud to be a supporter of Circles and can't wait to watch this business grow!

A hot, fresh, in-house aged and spiced Pastrami on fresh rye at Katz's Deli is around the price of what you pay at F&M. The problem is that F&M gets their meat from a mass producer of meat and it sits in a case, cold, until you buy it and they slice it thin. Where F & M fails is that the ingredients are just regular, run of the mill packaged deli meat. Nothing fresh. On a trip in December 2019, food in the case was spotted with mold on it. There is a leak from the condenser in the case that leaks water into the case. Flies are flying all around. I have worked in a deli and saw the signs of food (various salads) not getting much turn over. The service was not much better. Slow, disorganized, and not too friendly. Overall, I would avoid. text: I've been visiting The Butterfly House since they first opened their doors many years ago, and I still love coming here! There's nothing quite like taking a moment to relax, smell the flowers, and witness thousands of butterflies flutter free throughout the greenhouse. Some of the butterflies will get pretty friendly and fly near enough to your face that you just feel a whisp of their wings. Even bolder butterflies will take a few moments to land on your hands or body. They are incredibly interesting to watch if you're into insects, and it is a photographer's dream inside. I've had the pleasure of photographing a wedding here as well, and The Butterfly House staff do a wonderful job organizing everything and working with vendors. My bride even had some butterflies land on her arm the day of her wedding, which was so special to document! A few tips: * If you are bringing elderly folks who have breathing problems, they may be uncomfortable for long durations in The Butterfly House due to the humidity. * February and March are a great time to go to the Butterfly House since they host extra beautiful Blue Morphos for Mardi Gras (it used to be called Morpho Madness for March Madness back in the day). * There are other insects to check out along the walls before you get to the butterflies, so don't forget to check them out too! * At the end of The Butterfly House walking path there is a glass case full of live chrysalis. Be sure to check them out and see what is hatching! * There is an informational video available, and the volunteer at the ticket counter will be able to inform you when it will be starting next.

text: Ok y'all. I don't claim to be an expert on Mediterranean cuisine, at all. However, I have made my rounds in the USA and Europe, as well as enjoying home cooked meals made by friends who are natives of the region. It's one of my favorite cuisines and I can never get enough. So when mi amor told me about this place, I couldn't wait to try them out. OMG THE BEST Mediterranean food in the STL metropolitan area is right here! There are lots of vegan options, but no vegan/veggie combo platter so you'll just have to a la carte yourself a meal until they rectify that. FALAFEL- definitely one of the best I've ever had. I always test this by trying the falafel by itself. Expectations = exceeded. Crispy outside, warm, tender, and with a hint of spice inside, along with an excellent combination of seasoning. Pure perfection. BABA GANOUSH - creamy, savory, and flavorful with just the right amount of olive oil. Another top contender in the STL! HUMMUS - smooth, creamy, and delectable, also with a just amount of olive oil. Again, one of the best you'll find! GRAPE LEAVES (aka dolmas) - the menu states these are made with meat. I called to see if they had a vegan version and was told yes, they make them without meat. Now, I don't know if they're always made like this, so be sure to ask, and then double check. They were delicious. I particularly like how they roll theirs small and thin. It's the perfect appetizer portion so you're not too full to eat the rest of your food. SPICY POTATO SALAD (aka batata harra) - diced potatoes cooked with mouthwatering spices. Very good! STUFFED SPINACH PIES - when I found out theirs is made without cheese AND is vegan, I was shook! SHOOKETH! So it's bread stuffed with spinach and onions. It's simple yet so good, y'all! ZA'ATAR MANAQISH - flatbread with a za'atar spread that is olive oil based instead of butter based. A hearty, robust flavor that pairs well with salads or own its own. Yummy. Every single item I ordered was superb. I also have to mention the tahini and hot sauce, because they're winning on their own. I will pay for extra on my next visit. They give you plenty of pita bread for your meal too. The employees were extremely nice and hospitable. I felt like family! The owner was very kind and patient with me as I respectfully grilled him about what was vegan. My only wish is that they consider adding a veggie combo meal and maybe a vegan dessert or two in the future. Meanwhile, I'll be frequenting to get my Mediterranean food fix.

text: First review about this place and I may edit if my experience changes: It is our Beagle's first week here. Before we moved to Reno, NV, we had paid a visit to Pet Play House and explained the situation to them. We travel a lot and need a safe/friendly place where the dog eventually feels comfortable just like where he used to go before we moved to Reno. The entire place seems well maintained including their overnight boarding areas, pet play areas, and common areas. The lobby is inviting, and the staff seems friendly. On my dog's first day there, he was obviously nervous, everything is new to him including the house, surroundings, people, and the daycare. He did bark a bit but it looks like the staff took it slow and eased him into the whole strenuous experience. We took a break next day and took him back there again and he jumped out of the car eager to go in and make friends again. The second time we took him there was better - he greeted the friendly girl who he met last time and it seems to be going okay. They gave him a really cute report about how his day went that we both found really funny. To most people, this review will be overly informative, but to those with dogs that are fearful/anxious, let me tell you know incredibly important it is to have such an establishment around. It is a sure-shot way to socialize them and tire them out in the process. I'm excited about eventually trying to board him there overnight and that should ease all our worries when we travel out of town. I continue to look forward to making Bagel a part of your amazing play house. My wife and I are forever grateful to you and your staff already :)

text: Two years ago I bought a 2009 Prius. The interior is like new. Pock marks and pitting marred the front hood. The clear coat degraded on the roof and sides. I finally made a decision to get quotes from well established auto body painters with good reputations in Tampa for decades. The quotes I received were between $5-9,000. That was well over my budget. I paid less than that for the car. All the long timers recommended I stay away from companies like Maaco. They told me my car had to be taken down to the metal and the hood blasted and that Maaco wouldn't do that plus the job wouldn't last. I began to watch you tube videos of a wide variety of cars and trucks painted two years ago or longer by Maaco. The work looked great. I decided to get a quote. My rep Manny was cordial, professional and explained the various priced packages and warranties leaving it up to me to make the final choice without any pressure! I liked his approach. I read the recent reviews on Yelp for this location and they were very positive. I chose a mid level package and Manny added some additional time for taking the hood down to metal, fixing other minor cosmetic scratches on the front and rear bumpers. I left the car on Monday and got a call Thursday morning that it was ready. When I arrived by Uber and saw my car I couldn't believe what outstanding work Maaco had done. Everything Manny promised was completed to my satisfaction. Now, my Prius looks like it just came off the showroom floor! One doesn't need to over pay for good work! It can be done and you can save thousands of dollars plus I have a full warranty on workmanship. I was introduced to Ivan, the owner, who has been painting cars here for over 30 years. This is a family business. His son works with him as well. They have a team of talented people. Saying thanks seems inadequate. I can't tell you enough how proud I am to drive my car. It's simply outstanding. Continued success!

text: This is a copy of my review for the Santa Barbara location, but is relevant for Goleta as well: I've been a long-time member at Massage Envy (since 2008) and have booked treatments at both the Goleta and SB locations. This review is with regards to the interaction I had with the manager, Brittany Jourdan and the regional franchisee director, Sarah Alhadithi. I have struggled over the years to get appointment times that fit my schedule, resulting in an accrual of massage "credits". I would occasionally take self-care days from work and book multiple treatments to try to use them up, but these were unfortunately uncommon. I would call weekly and check online for openings, and was frequently told that "regulars" had standing appointments so they couldn't accommodate any times that worked for me. I repeatedly told staff that I work an 8-5 office job and couldn't leave mid-day, but those were typically the only appointments offered. I tried to see what appointments were available even several weeks and months ahead, and was told they didn't have enough therapists staffed to accommodate me. I requested to cancel my membership and asked to get a credit back for my unused massages since I could not get appointment times. I was told it was against their franchise policy to provide a refund back without approval from their regional franchisee director or the owner. Emails back forth spanning a total of 2.5 weeks resulted in the franchisee director telling me that they would in no way refund my unused massages and that I had 60 days to use them, but they'd be happy to extend that another 30 days if needed. Suspiciously a week after my initial complaints to the manager, they magically had staff available for my preferred times. At this point, I'm really mad at the interaction, lack of customer service, and the priority of putting profits over doing the right thing for a long-standing customer. I will do my best to use my unused credits but will be warning anyone looking for a massage to avoid this place like the plague.

text: Horrible Experience-Hair Ruined-Zero Accountability I have never written a bad review online before, but felt that it was necessary for others to know what I went through before choosing Salon West to color your hair. I was very happy the first two times I went in for a full color. The third time I went, I told my stylist that some of the hair around my face/bang area were breaking off. She told me it was normal and to switch part sides and use a conditioner called Olaplex 3, which I bought. She colored my hair that day and it looked very light, but ok. As the week went on, my hair began breaking all over. It seemed to have started at the front, but then became more widespread, breaking at all different lengths all over my head. I became concerned and decided to go and see a referral of a friend who was a stylist of 25 years. He did nothing but give me Olaplex 6 and told me not to come for a while to allow my hair a break. I decided to call the owner of the salon, at the time not looking for anything in return, but to let them know, so it wouldn't happen to another. Instead of the owner, a customer service rep. called me. I told him what had happened and that I just wanted to let him know so they stylist could get the training needed so it wouldn't happen to others. He asked if he could call me back the next day after looking into it. I told him it wasn't necessary, but he persisted. He called me back the next day and told me that he looked over the stylist's notes and that she had done everything right and it was probably that my hair couldn't handle the color. I have been this color for years! I told him I thought that was the stylists job to know what a client's hair can and cannot handle, but he stuck to his guns and instead offered me a complimentary conditioning treatment. A couple more weeks went by and my hair just kept breaking and getting worse. I decided to call and ask for the owner to please call me back, as I was starting to get very upset about the condition of my hair, and I wanted her to know that I didn't think it was right that I was told my hair was to blame instead of the Salon taking responsibility. I received no call back. Another two weeks went by and I decided to try her one more time and left a detailed message for her. No phone call back. I figured she must have no idea how bad my hair had actually become. It is completely ruined with uneven, broken pieces all over and feels like straw. I asked my new hair dresser if I should get it cut to a bob, but he told me no matter what, it will continue breaking unevenly and wouldn't make sense to have it shorter and doing that. Before I was going to write the review I decided to call the customer service rep. one last time to give them the benefit of the doubt and offer to go to the salon and show them my hair. I am obviously feeling very self-conscious and emotional about the state of my hair and felt no one seemed to care at Salon West. He called me back and left a voicemail telling me that he had spoken with the owner and that because my last treatment was so long ago (June) and that I chose to go to another salon, all they could offer was $90 refund for my last color. He apologized for causing the breakage! I was insulted and angry and sad all at once. They weren't interested in seeing my completely ruined hair, which took me 4 years to grow. I wasn't interested in getting my $90 dollars back! I was interested in hearing that the owner wanted to speak with me or that they wanted to look at my hair to see what I was talking about and how they might help in the slow growing back process. text: Employees are rude, don't seem to know what they're doing, and will lie to you to make a sale. My mother and I have plans to completely transform our backyard into a sort of edible plant oasis and wanted to visit a few different nurseries to get an idea for what was available before committing to a plan. We heard very good things about Jene's and wanted to visit the store while we were out and about one day. We were disappointed almost immediately. Walking around the very small lot, we noticed that most of the trees are located behind a roped off area. They are labeled either with a small tag on the tree, or on the container they are planted in. But the tags can't be read from far away (or even close up, really), and many of the labels on the containers weren't facing the walking path, or just simply weren't there at all. We flagged down an employee with the hope of finding out exactly what kind of trees there were on the lot, but as we were halfway through our question, she left abruptly, without a word, to go help someone else. Fine, we thought, they must be very busy. We waited a couple minutes and she returned, ready to hear our question. Once again, halfway through our question, she left abruptly, without a word, to go do something else. Odd, but my mother and I assumed that something important must be going on and we wandered around as best we could, even though we had managed to view everything we possibly could, very, very quickly. The employee returned and left abruptly in the middle of our question a couple more times after that. Finally, she came back again and we managed to get through the sentence. We finally got to ask her what kinds of plants were available in the store. The woman, however, only showed us the varieties that could be seen from the walking path, which weren't many varieties at all. We asked her what were the plants behind the rope, and she gave us some sheets of paper that list the varieties of citrus, avocado, and mango that they had. That's great and all, but we had also seen some trees that appeared to be something other than citrus, avocado, or mango, and wanted to know what they were. Despite asking, we never got a clear answer. I asked her out of curiosity if they had a very rare, nearly extinct banana tree called Gros Michel. I didn't expect them to have it, and it would have been fine if they didn't, but I had seen some other nurseries in Florida claim to have the Gros Michel and wanted to know, on the off chance, if they did too. The woman told me that they didn't have it, and that was fine. She then asked us what we were going to buy. We explained that we didn't plan on buying anything that day, but would probably come back next week after we research the varieties on the papers she had given us. She seemed very irritated, and tried to convince us that the trees we wanted would be gone by next week. We told her that that was fine, and decided to wander the store one last time before leaving. As we wandered, we saw her with another employee, and she pointed us out to this other employee, said something in another language to him, and they both laughed hysterically at us. She and the other employee then rushed over to us and told us that they do in fact have Gros Michel bananas, but pointed to the bananas labeled Gran Nain. We told her no, they are different bananas, but she insisted that they were Gros Michel, all while laughing like a hyena with the other employee. We left immediately after that, horrified. We will be looking elsewhere for our plants.
label: NEG

text: I always thought Webster Groves ER Hospital was top notch. At least that's what I'd heard in the past. On Sunday my cat became ill. I noticed she felt hot and thought she had fever. I rushed her to Webster Groves (I am grateful they offer this service on a Sunday). They did an evaluation and prescribed a liquid antibiotic and gave her some fluids to try to reduce the fever. Once I got home I realized that the medication we were given for a 9 pound cat was going to require me to get 4 milliliters of liquid medicine in my cat twice per day. That is 8 total milliliters of liquid per day that I was instructed to give with a syringe. The syringe does not even fit in the medicine bottle I was given. No adapter was provided. I attempted to give this medication the first night and the next morning. After my cat spit every bit of this bubble gum smelling mess all over my house she was traumatized from me essentially drowning her with this medicine. I tried calling the clinic to explain and ask questions. I spoke with Cierra who put me on hold for a tech. My call rang back to Cierra at least 3 times, because I held for so long that no one took my call. After my 3rd attempt at talking with Cierra - she told me that a tech must not be available. I asked if we could just discuss the problem. She quickly told me she is not medically trained and I needed to just wait. She then put someone else on the phone - who also did not listen. I was trying to explain that I have never nor has anyone I know ever been asked to give more than 1 ML of medicine at a time to any cat. I tried to explain I've given Clavamox drops to my other cat on multiple occasions. It was assumed because I mentioned this that I was requesting Clavamox drops for my cat that is sick now. I WAS NOT. I want her to be on the correct medication and I wanted to have a conversation with someone about it. I was not asking for the medication to be changed - I was trying to ask for it to be given to me MIXED APPROPRIATELY for a cat. Medicines come in concentrates. You mix it appropriate to the size of the animal. Your Vibramycin supply is mixed for a much smaller animal than a cat. No cat should ever receive more than 1 ML of medication per dose. NO ONE at your clinic of any authority would even speak to me on this matter. This was an error in your prescribing or in your pharmacy and I really hope that this is not done to someone with less animal handling experience. I was ultimately given Doxycycline TABLETS for my cat instead of this incorrectly mixed Vibramycin liquid. No one would take responsibility for this error or even admit that it was an error. I should have been given a pill OR liquid option from the beginning. I was never asked what might be best for my cat. I was ultimately given the Doxycycline tablets for my cat at no charge and sent on my way. That tells me they understand they made an error and it's unfortunate that I could not be given the opportunity to have a face to face conversation about this with the doctor that prescribed the medication. Very frustrating experience and my cat was sick with a fever for an extra day because of this. The woman at the pharmacy window did hear me out and try to help me the best that she could (in person) but I could tell she was limited by what she was allowed to say to me. Of course she cannot make her own place of employment look as if they made an error. Errors happen and are acceptable; we are human after all - it's how you address them when they arise that counts. I will never be back to your clinic. All I wanted was someone to slow down and listen to what had happened so that this does not happen to anyone else's cat.

I said well, it was perfectly tight, never loose before THEY re-sized it. Not only that, but it appears they may have gotten some adhesive (or something) clearly visible on the moonstone itself. So for $50, they basically destroyed my $700 irreplaceable one of kind beautiful moonstone ring that I likely will never be able to fully trust wearing again, nor appreciate again as the stone itself looks damaged, and I'm scared to try to clean it in case the "adhesive" shifts anywhere else. . No refund offer for re-sizing and while I REALLY should have demanded one, at that point I just wanted to leave. I had already wasted too much of my time and energy. I likely would have come back to broken prongs that I'm sure would have also been the ring's fault. Needless to say I left, and shall never return.
